subject: Urgent: Hosted API tail latency spike — exec briefing & mitigation
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@aurelia-labs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Cho <michael.cho@aurelia-labs.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 13:42:11 +0000
Subject: High P99 tail latency from Hosted API affecting batch inference — immediate assistance required

Hi Hannah,

We're seeing a severe degradation on the Hosted API that started around 12:30 UTC and is still ongoing. Our nightly batch inference jobs (concurrent jobs: 12) are seeing P95 jump from ~180ms to ~1.1s and P99 spikes above 4.5s. Error rate (5xx) has also trended up from 0.03% to ~1.4% during the window.

Impact:
- Customer facing: downstream enrichment pipeline stalls, downstream retry floods our own queues.
- SLAs: we're on a production contract and this is blocking our end-of-day reporting.

We've attached a short trace sample and the agent logs. We suspect something in the batching/backpressure layer is building up queues — several requests are showing queue_wait > 800ms before token generation begins.

Can a Redwood engineer join an incident call now? Our SRE (Michael) is available for a 15–30 min war room. We need mitigation (rollback/traffic-shift) and an action plan for next 24 hours. If you need procurement or legal added for credits, loop them in.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of ML Platform | Aurelia Labs

Attachments: aurelia_tail_latency_logs_2026-05-21.zip, p99-sample-trace-20260521.json
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@aurelia-labs.com>
Cc: Michael Cho <michael.cho@aurelia-labs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 13:48:02 +0000
Subject: Re: High P99 tail latency from Hosted API affecting batch inference — immediate assistance required

Thanks for the heads up, Lena — I’m sorry you’re hitting this.

Neha & Dylan: can you triage now? Please confirm whether this is: a) circuit/backpressure misconfig, b) batching window growth due to traffic pattern, or c) a runtime kernel regression. Attach any quick mitigations you intend to deploy (and ETA).

Lena/Michael: joining a call now makes sense — sharing a temporary conference link: meet.redwood.com/incident-aurelia-0521 (15 minute slot booked).

I’ve attached the logs you sent into our incident folder and pulled the initial Kibana snapshot. I’ll keep execs looped but want a short technical summary before escalating.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan_Aurelia_20260521.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@aurelia-labs.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 14:02:35 +0000
Subject: Re: High P99 tail latency from Hosted API affecting batch inference — immediate assistance required

Quick technical summary from initial triage (15:02 UTC):

Observed signals:
- P95/P99 divergence begins ~12:28 UTC aligned with a brief traffic burst from Aurelia (concurrent sessions + wide sequence length variance).
- Queue depth metric (hosted-proxy.queue_depth) increased from baseline ~2–6 to sustained 40–70 on a small subset of instance shards.
- Batching window averaged 28ms -> 180ms on affected shards (we batch up to window_max_ms to improve throughput; window can grow when admissions outpace token generation).
- KV cache thrash: token cache hit ratio dropped 14% -> 3% on the same shards, likely due to model routing mixing multiple user sessions (sequence length variance causes cache churn).
- No kernel-level exceptions or OOMs observed. 5xxs correlate with client timeouts after long queue_waits rather than server process failure.

Probable root cause hypothesis:
- Workload change (Aurelia’s batch jobs) exposed a corner in our batching admission: sustained high queue depth + long batching window -> elevated tail latency for single-request latency-sensitive paths. In short, backlog grows faster than tokens are emitted on a few shards, pushing p99 up.

Immediate mitigations (rolling within 5–15 minutes):
1) Reduce batching window_max_ms on affected pool from 200ms -> 10ms to prioritize latency over throughput (impact: ~8–12% cost increase for affected requests).
2) Trigger emergency scale-up for dedicated hosted pool + add 2x worker replicas for 30 minutes to clear backlog.
3) Apply a temporary per-account concurrency cap for Aurelia (limit concurrent sessions from their API key to 8) to prevent admission storms.
4) Enable fallback routing: route their requests to a compatible lighter-quantized model variant for any new sessions during the incident window.

Next steps (post-incident):
- Postmortem with timeline + corrective engineering to prevent batching window runaway (change: admission token and KV affinity improvements).
- Propose a targeted quantization/profile for Aurelia workload and a recommended concurrency SLO in our onboarding docs.

I’ll start the rolling changes now (plan: deploy change to canary shards at 14:06, evaluate, roll). Will update in 10 minutes with observed delta on p95/p99 and queue_depth.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 14:20:53 +0000
Subject: Exec brief: Aurelia Labs hosted-p99 incident — proposed customer remediation

Marissa/Sean — quick summary and ask for approval:

What happened: Hosted API experienced sustained p99 latency spikes beginning 12:28 UTC for customer Aurelia Labs. Root cause likely batching/queue depth growth on a subset of shards that caused long queue_wait times and elevated 5xxs as clients timed out.

What we did:
- Applied immediate mitigations per Neha: reduced batching window on canary -> full roll in ~12m; emergency scale-up + per-account concurrency cap; fallback to quantized variant for new sessions.
- Cleared backlog within ~20 minutes; p95 returned to ~230ms, p99 down to ~600–800ms; error-rate returned to baseline.

Customer impact: Several EOD jobs delayed; Aurelia requested incident call and remediation.

Proposed customer remediation:
1) 7.5% credit on May invoice (one-off) to address SLA miss and operational burden.
2) Offer a free workload-tuning engagement (2x SE days) to tune batching/quantization and a recommended config for their production jobs.

Ask: Approve the proposed credit and SE engagement so I can confirm with Aurelia. If you prefer a different percent credit, please let me know ASAP — the customer is sensitive and requested exec-level visibility.

-Hannah
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@aurelia-labs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Cho <michael.cho@aurelia-labs.com>, procure@aurelia-labs.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:05:18 +0000
Subject: Re: Exec brief: Aurelia Labs hosted-p99 incident — proposed customer remediation

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the quick response and the temporary mitigations. The p99 reduction you reported looks good from our end.

We accept the offer for the tuning engagement; procurement will reach out separately about the credit and updated order terms. For now, please proceed with the SE session and schedule a working review next week (prefer Tue/Wed morning UTC).

Thanks,
Lena
